span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We argue that this is primarily caused by the practice of order splitting, in which large institutional funds split their trading orders into many small pieces.

span.label: market impact and long-memory of order flow
span.quote: By market impact we mean the average response of prices to trades; liquidity refers to the scale of the market impact

span.label: review
span.quote: In this article we revisit the classic problem of tatonnement in price formation from a microstructure point of view, reviewing a recent body of theoretical and empirical work explaining how fluctuations in supply and demand are slowly incorporated into prices.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM IS COINED BY AN OPERATIONAL TEST RATHER THAN BY A DESCRIPTION, FOR OBJECTS THAT DO NOT COME PRE-SORTED: to treat these different types **IN A UNIFIED MANNER** we classify them **BASED ON WHETHER AN ORDER RESULTS IN AN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION**, in which case **WE CALL IT AN EFFECTIVE MARKET ORDER**, or whether it leaves a limit order sitting in the book, in which case **WE CALL IT AN EFFECTIVE LIMIT ORDER**. The definition is a procedure a reader could run, and it replaces the types the paper started from with a classification produced by an outcome
span.quote: In order to treat these different types simply and in a unified manner we simply classify them based on whether an order results in an immediate transaction, in which case we call it an effective market order, or whether it leaves a limit order sitting in the book, in which case we call it an effective limit order.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THEN THE QUALIFIER IS DROPPED BY ANNOUNCEMENT, SO THE FIELD'S ORDINARY WORD NOW DENOTES THE AUTHORS' CONSTRUCT: **NOTE THAT WE TYPICALLY DROP THE TERM “EFFECTIVE”**, so that e.g. **“MARKET ORDER” MEANS “EFFECTIVE MARKET ORDER”**. The redefinition of an existing term is stated as a notational convenience, in one sentence, and every later use of the word carries it
span.quote: Note that we typically drop the term “effective”, so that e.g. “market order” means “effective market order”.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A THREE-WORD COMPOUND TERM IS DEFINED ONE WORD AT A TIME, EACH WORD GIVEN ITS OWN CLAUSE: **“AUCTION” INDICATES** that participants may place quotes stating the quantities and prices at which they are willing to trade; **“CONTINUOUS” INDICATES** that they can update, cancel or place new quotes at any time; and **“DOUBLE” INDICATES** that the market is symmetric between buyers and sellers. The name of the institution is decomposed into three separately checkable properties
span.quote: “Auction” indicates that participants may place quotes (also called orders) stating the quantities and prices at which they are willing to trade; “continuous” indicates that they can update, cancel or place new quotes at any time, and “double” indicates that the market is symmetric between buyers and sellers

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHETHER A CENTRAL CONCEPT IS VALID AT ALL IS ASKED AS A QUESTION, WITH COMPUTABILITY AS THE CRITERION: **IS THE FUNDAMENTAL VALUE OF A STOCK OR A CURRENCY A VALID CONCEPT**, in the sense that it **CAN BE COMPUTED, AT LEAST AS A MATTER OF PRINCIPLE, WITH ARBITRARY ACCURACY** with all information known at the time? The test proposed for whether a term denotes anything is whether a number could in principle be produced for it
span.quote: Is the fundamental value of a stock or a currency a valid concept, in the sense that it can be computed, at least as a matter of principle, with arbitrary accuracy with all information known at time t?

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: VAGUENESS IS DECLARED INTENTIONAL, AND REMOVING IT IS NAMED AS THE POINT OF THE CHAPTER: **WE ARE INTENTIONALLY BEING VAGUE AT THIS STAGE ABOUT THE DEFINITION** of the return and the volume; **DEFINING THESE MORE PRECISELY IS ONE OF THE MAIN POINTS OF THIS CHAPTER**. The imprecision is positioned as a stage of the argument rather than as a defect of it
span.quote: We are intentionally being vague at this stage about the definition of the return R and the volume V ; defining these more precisely is one of the main points of this chapter.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN EQUATION IS WRITTEN AND THEN DECLARED NOT TO BE READ LITERALLY, WITH THE TWO PROPERTIES IT ASSERTS BOTH DENIED: the above equation **SHOULD BE INTERPRETED RATHER LOOSELY**: as we shall see below, **IMPACT IS IN FACT NEITHER LINEAR NOR PERMANENT**. The formalism is retained as an expository device after its content has been withdrawn
span.quote: Furthermore, the above equation should be interpreted rather loosely: as we shall see below, impact is in fact neither linear nor permanent.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A SCARE-QUOTED TERM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SENTENCE: a very important empirical fact is that **EVEN “HIGHLY LIQUID” MARKETS ARE IN FACT NOT THAT LIQUID**. The quotation marks mark the received usage and the clause after them denies it, so the word survives with its reference reversed
span.quote: A very important empirical fact that is crucial to understand how markets operate is that even “highly liquid” markets are in fact not that liquid.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A DEFINITION'S OWN STRICTNESS IS ASSESSED BY THE PEOPLE WHO WROTE IT: **BY REQUIRING THAT ANY ASSOCIATED ALTERATIONS OF ORDERS BE CONSIDERED INFORMATION, WE HAVE TAKEN A VERY STRICT DEFINITION** of mechanical impact. The boundary of the term is traced back to the requirement that produced it, and the requirement is named
span.quote: By requiring that any associated alterations of orders be considered information, we have taken a very strict definition of mechanical impact.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A QUANTITY IS DEFINED BY A COUNTERFACTUAL NOBODY CAN STAGE, AND THE IMPOSSIBILITY IS PART OF THE DEFINITION: **WE DEFINE A MECHANICAL IMPACT AS WHAT HAPPENS IF SOMEONE PLACES AN ORDER** in the order book **IF THIS ORDER HAS NO EFFECT ON ANY FUTURE ORDERS** - we are essentially asking what happens **IF AN ORDER IS INJECTED INTO THE ORDER BOOK AT RANDOM, BUT NO ONE PAYS ANY ATTENTION TO IT**. The term denotes the outcome of an intervention the market makes impossible by responding
span.quote: We define a mechanical impact as what happens if someone places an order in the order book if this order has no effect on any future orders. We are essentially asking the question of what happens to the price if an order is injected into the order book at random, but no one pays any attention to it.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM IS DEFINED BY WHAT THE AGENTS CANNOT KNOW, NOT BY WHAT IS THE CASE: **WE CALL THIS INFORMATION SET ANONYMOUS BECAUSE** liquidity providers **DO NOT KNOW THE IDENTITY** of the liquidity takers and **ARE UNABLE TO ESTABLISH WHETHER OR NOT TWO DIFFERENT ORDERS COME FROM THE SAME TRADER**. The property named is an absence in someone's knowledge, and the definition says whose
span.quote: We call this information set anonymous because liquidity providers do not know the identity of the liquidity takers and are unable to establish whether or not two different orders come from the same trader.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MECHANISM IS COINED AND ITS TWO HALVES ARE STATED AS A CONCESSION AND A QUALIFICATION: **WE CALL THIS MECHANISM ASYMMETRIC LIQUIDITY**: each transaction **HAS A PERMANENT IMPACT**, but the impact **DEPENDS ON THE PAST ORDER FLOW AND ON ITS PREDICTABILITY**. The name is minted for a claim that concedes the standard result and then makes it conditional
span.quote: We call this mechanism asymmetric liquidity: each transaction has a permanent impact, but the impact depends on the past order flow and on its predictability.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A COMPARISON IS DECLARED MISLEADING UNLESS A THEORY THE FIELD DOES NOT HAVE IS SUPPLIED FIRST: for this reason it is in general **MISLEADING TO COMPARE AGGREGATE IMPACT CURVES WITH DIFFERENT SCALES**, **UNLESS ONE HAS A THEORY FOR HOW THE MARKET IMPACT DEPENDS ON AGGREGATION SCALE**. The condition on a valid comparison is named, and it is a theory rather than a measurement
span.quote: For this reason it is in general misleading to compare aggregate impact curves with different scales, unless one has a theory for how the market impact depends on aggregation scale.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A DEFINITION IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE FIELD AND QUALIFIED BY WHICH SENSE OF THE WORD IT DEFINES: **A STANDARD DEFINITION OF MARKET EFFICIENCY (IN THE INFORMATIONAL SENSE)** is that the current price should be **THE BEST PREDICTOR OF FUTURE PRICES**, i.e. that prices should be a martingale. The parenthesis concedes that the term has other senses, and the definition is scoped to one of them
span.quote: A standard definition of market efficiency (in the informational sense) is that the current price should be the best predictor of future prices, i.e. that prices should be a martingale.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND A SECOND SENSE OF THE SAME WORD IS GIVEN ITS OWN STRICT DEFINITION, IN OTHER PEOPLE'S VOCABULARY: **STRICTLY SPEAKING A MARKET IS ALLOCATIVELY EFFICIENT IF IT IS PARETO OPTIMAL**. One word given a second technical sense, defined strictly and in another field's vocabulary
span.quote: Strictly speaking a market is allocatively efficient if it is Pareto optimal

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MEASUREMENT THE FIELD RELIES ON IS SAID TO HAVE NO GOOD METHOD, AND THE SUBSTITUTE IS NAMED AS ROUGH: **UNFORTUNATELY THERE ARE STILL NOT GOOD STATISTICAL METHODS FOR ASSIGNING CONFIDENCE INTERVALS FOR EXPONENTS OF POWER LAWS**, particularly when the observations have long-memory - but **THE ERRORS CAN BE ROUGHLY ASSESSED BY EXAMINING SUB-SAMPLES**. The exponents are quoted throughout the literature; the uncertainty on them is admitted to be unavailable
span.quote: Unfortunately there are still not good statistical methods for assigning confidence intervals for exponents of power laws, particularly when the observations have long-memory, but the errors can be roughly assessed by examining sub-samples.

span.quote: The work described here is still in an early stage, and is very much in flux; many of these results are quite new and indeed our own view is still changing as new results appear.

span.label: The market-ecology picture lacks the comprehensive empirical study it would need, because databases linking participants to strategies are hard to obtain.
span.quote: It would be extremely valuable to have a comprehensive empirical study that connects the heterogeneity of market participants with their strategy and with the properties of price dynamics.

span.quote: This means that there is no reason to believe that instantaneous prices are equilibrium, efficient prices that reflect all known information. Much of the information is necessarily latent, withheld due to the small liquidity of the market, and only slowly revealing itself

We have no type for it: `causes` asserts production, and `operationalised-as` says the authors CHOSE a measure, whereas a proxy claim says THIS STANDS IN FOR WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT AND WE KNOW IT IS NOT THE SAME THING. Measured at 8% of papers. A proxy held UNDER A THEORY, not asserted: 'UNDER THE THEORY THAT urgency is a proxy for informativeness, empirical work on the subject has often defined an informed trade as one that is executed by a market order'. The whole downstream definition depends on a substitution the sentence flags as theoretical.
span.quote: For example, under the theory that urgency is a proxy for informativeness, empirical work on the subject has often defined an informed trade as one that is executed by a market order, and defined an uninformed trade as one that is represented by a limit order.
